protected_invariants: the independent reviewer stays independent: it is a fresh separate Codex context, launched by the canonical runner, reading a clean detached read-only exact-head worktree, and it never reuses a Builder session or Builder context

the exact reviewed head is preserved: a receipt is only ever bound to the full 40-character SHA it reviewed, a short, abbreviated, trailing-space, non-hex or empty --head-sha is refused rather than guessed

the receipt remains the single authority for the reviewed verdict: stdout, the printed status line and the process exit status are projections of the receipt and are never an independent source of the verdict, and a receipt edited after sealing fails its recomputed integrity digest and is refused
the evidence directory stays owner-only (0700) and every receipt stays owner-only (0600) and owned by the current uid, on the reading side and the writing side, under one shared rule
P0, P1 and P2 findings block merge readiness, and stale tooling can never satisfy it: STALE_TOOLING keeps historical audit meaning only and CURRENT_PR_REVIEW + STALE_TOOLING stays MERGE_READY=NO
a receipt for a head other than the reviewed head is refused, and a receipt for a superseded head is refused and reported as an explicit RECEIPT_MISSING failure rather than waited out

one head may carry several review rounds, so a verdict must name the round it belongs to: a receipt of another round is never consumed as this round's verdict, and mtime ordering alone is never treated as round identity

PID reuse protection stays intact: a writer is identified by its pid together with its /proc start time as recorded at launch, a non-positive --pid is refused, a bare --pid with no start time is refused, and an unusable liveness hint is never read as evidence of the writer's death

the repository wait layer has no human wake-up dependency: one blocking command establishes the verdict, and an abnormal reviewer exit, a missing receipt or a timeout ends in an explicit failure state instead of silently returning control

invalid input is a structured refusal and not a crash: an unusable --head-sha or --run-id ends in REVIEW_FAILED with exit 1 and, under --json, one JSON line on stdout, never a traceback whose meaning must be parsed out of stderr

the direct Python entrypoint keeps the full classification (0 = reviewed PASS with no blocking finding, 3 = reviewed FAIL or any blocking finding, 1 = no verdict could be established), while GNU make only promises that a PASS is 0 and that anything else is non-zero; exact classification through make is read from the printed JSON, and make's exit status is not hacked to carry a child's 3
no business, provider, database, deployment or Stage D surface is touched: BLOCKER_3 stays CLOSED, GATE_2 stays ACCEPTED, GATE_3 stays NOT_AUTHORIZED and STAGE_D_STARTED stays NO

the pre-existing execution contract of the repository is unchanged: no required check is weakened, no Gatekeeper rule or validation profile is loosened, and no test that guards an accepted invariant is deleted or made vacuous

merging any pull request, including this one, which stops at the merge gate without a new Controller authorization
contacting The Odds API, Backblaze B2, AWS, Cloudflare or any other remote provider, and consuming any provider quota
creating any backup generation, executing any restore, mutating provider data, or touching backup and restore production logic
starting Stage D, activating any scheduler, applying any migration, and creating, requesting, reading, printing or persisting any credential or secret value
changing Stage D provider logic, The Odds API integration, bookmaker registry business logic, database schema, deployment configuration, unrelated CI, or betting and value logic
weakening, bypassing or suppressing any required check, including the Gatekeeper long-file rule, the changed-line static quality gate and the AI Workflow Gate mission scope enforcement
adding a new runtime dependency, or changing package.json or package-lock.json
hacking GNU make's exit status to preserve a child process's exact exit code, or documenting that make preserves a classification it cannot carry
